skills: Year 1
Reading with a pencil: annotate, summarise every chapter in three lines, and keep the reading log from the first week of ENG 113, ENG 114 and ENG 115.
Paragraphs that make one point with evidence - the Writing pair (ENG 101 / ENG 102 / ENG 103, by placement), then ENG 201 Composition II.
The vocabulary of literature and of linguistics (ENG 111 Principles of Linguistics, ENG 123 History of English Language).
Speaking in class once every session; the programme page says student tutors support the 100-level courses - use them.
Year 2
Close reading of a poem, a scene and a page of prose on the page, not from summaries (the surveys ENG 213, ENG 214, ENG 215; ENG 217 Shakespeare).
A first linguistics dataset: a conversation transcribed for ENG 211, child language for ENG 212 or ENG 315, a Bangladeshi text for ENG 221.
An essay process you repeat every time: question, thesis statement, outline, draft, revise, cite.
One citation style used correctly in every essay, and a quotation bank with page numbers.
Year 3

Your specialisation's spine: Literature's surveys and ENG 319 Modernism; ELT's ENG 242 The Study of English, ENG 327 Second Language Acquisition and ENG 334 ELT Methodology; Media's ENG 205, ENG 320, ENG 331 and ENG 333.
Research with secondary sources and a theory lens - ENG 301 Research Methodology works through Marxism, feminism, postcolonialism and psychoanalysis.

A lesson you have actually taught (ENG 332 Teaching Techniques) or a piece you have actually published (ENG 440 English for the Print Media; Resonance, the department's student-run bilingual journal).
A second string: translation (ENG 465), editing (ENG 401), copywriting (ENG 404) or creative writing (ENG 220).
Year 4
The dissertation (6 credits, equivalent to two courses) or the internship report, with a question narrow enough to answer in the word limit.

ENG 490 Seminar Course - weekly three-hour seminars on diversity, discrimination and inclusion in Bangladeshi society, completed in one semester - and the research paper ENG 480 Independent Reading Course ends in.
A portfolio of writing samples in three registers: academic, professional, public.
Applications, test scores and referees who have read your long work, lined up a semester early.
dept.career_intro: An English degree does not train you for one job; it makes you good at reading closely, writing clearly and explaining things to people, and your specialisation and your portfolio decide how employers read you. The programme page's placement section names 'B.A. Internships in various schools and media houses'. These are common directions, not BRACU rules.

Placement (freshman enrolment page): ENG 091 Foundation Course in English and MAT 091 / MAT 092 are non-credit; ENG 101 English Fundamentals and ENG 102 are 3 credits each; "Courses numbered 001-099 are remedial or non-credit courses".

Course load (university rule): freshmen take a maximum of 9 credits / 3 courses in the first semester; from the second semester the minimum is 9 and the maximum 15 credits, with 18 or more only as a department-recommended special case approved by the Dean/Chairperson and the Registrar.

The Residential Semester at Savar is compulsory for all BRAC University students, taken in the 3rd semester, and carries GenEd courses (the RS course page lists EMB 101, HUM 103, BU 201, ENG 102, BNG 103).

Degree rules: minimum CGPA 2.00 to graduate; at least 70 of the credits must be earned at BRAC University; probation below CGPA 2.0 (students enrolled Summer 2022 onward); maximum eight years from first admission.
Minors: the department offers a Minor in History (24 credits, open to students from diverse disciplines) and a Minor in English (27 credits = 9 courses; ENG 217 and ENG 301 compulsory).

Support: student tutors for the 100-level courses, the student-run bilingual creative writing journal Resonance, the ENH Seminar Series, and the department's Media Lab (digital audio and video editing).

book.text: Read this first

This planner puts your whole ENH degree in one place: every published course, the rules that move your CGPA, the dates that cost money, and a working page for every week of the semester - on your phone, offline, with the arithmetic done for you.
What you are holding

items: **Degree** - the Bachelor of Arts in English (BA in English) as BRACU prints it: every course, its credits and its prerequisite. Pick a semester and a grade per course and the CGPA, the credit map, the Ready / Locked checks and your semester-by-semester plan follow.
**CGPA** - the grading scale, a quick semester GPA, what it takes to reach a target, a retake what-if on BRACU's own rule, and the CGPA lines that decide waivers and standing.
**Money** - this semester's bill at the published rates, the whole degree roughly, and the dates that cost money with a countdown you can send to your calendar.
**Semester** - deadlines and tasks, your routine with a clash check, and the working pages of a semester (set-up, course pages, check-ins, finals plan), one set per semester.
**Toolkit** - the tools this department's work actually needs, with logs and calculators that count and flag as you type.
**Rules** - BRACU's own grading, retake, probation, load, scholarship and fee rules, with the source named under each.
**More** - clubs and careers, the printable pages, an assignment cover page, the Excel version of the tracker, and your backup.

book.text: What it is not

items: It is **not an official BRACU document**. Nobody at the university wrote, checked or approved it.
It does **not replace your advisor**, your advising sheet or the student portal. Those decide what counts toward your degree.

It is **a snapshot**. Course lists, fees, CGPA lines and dates were read from BRACU's own web pages on 20 October 2026. Universities change these. When a notice and this planner disagree - cross the old line out here, and the notice wins.

book.text: Start in 15 minutes

items: On **Home**, type your name, the semester you were admitted in and the semester you are in now.
On **Degree**, pick the semester and the grade of every course you have passed. Your CGPA appears at once, and every course shows Ready, Locked or Open.
On **Money**, type this semester's fee and drop dates from the Registrar's calendar; they count down on Home.
On **Semester**, put your sections into the routine and your deadlines into the task list.
Open the **Toolkit** when the work starts: labs, projects, cases, the final-year runway.

book.text: Your data

Everything you type stays in this browser on this device - nothing is sent anywhere, there is no account and no internet is needed. That also means a cleared browser or a new phone starts empty. So, now and then, open **More** and tap **Save this planner with my data inside**: you get this same file back with everything you have typed written into it. Keep that copy - open it on a laptop, send it to a new phone, or hand it to next semester's you.

If a browser refuses to keep your data between visits (some phones open files in a way that forgets), Home tells you so and offers the same button. Your planner is then simply the latest copy you saved.

Most students learn these rules by breaking one. Read them once now. Everything here is taken from BRAC University's published pages as they stood in October 2026; the source is named under each section.
The grading scale
BRAC University's undergraduate scale, in force since Fall 2020. Both A+ and A carry the full 4.0.
A+ to D- are passing grades. F is failing: it earns no credit and counts as zero in your GPA.
How your GPA and CGPA are worked out

Every course gives you **quality points = credits x grade point**. Add the quality points for a semester and divide by the credits you attempted for a letter grade: that is your semester GPA. Do the same across all semesters and you have your CGPA. The policy page prints the same formula: the sum of (grade points x credits) over the credits attempted.
Three things students get wrong

items: **An F stays in the sum until it is retaken.** It adds credits to the bottom of the fraction and nothing to the top.
**A D- passes, but it costs you.** A 3-credit D- is 2.1 quality points against 12.0 for an A - and a grade of B- or below is what the repeat rule exists for.
**W, I, P and AU never enter the GPA.** A W costs you the fee and the semester's work, not grade points.

book.text: 4. The essay runway and the thesis-statement builder
Essays go wrong at the question, not at the keyboard. Move every essay through the same six stations - and never start the draft until the thesis statement has passed the test below.

The whole thing written fast, body first, introduction last.
